::: {.callout-note}
## Simulated data

All numbers, names, and findings are **simulated**. The State of
Arcadonia does not exist.
:::

## Introduction

Tetanus is caused by toxin from *Clostridium tetani* contaminating
wounds. Disease is rare where childhood vaccination coverage is high,
but adults with waning immunity — especially those aged ≥65 years —
remain at risk. Reports and methodology notes are published by the
[Arcadonia Department of Public Health](https://example.org/arcadonia-health).

### Surveillance pipeline

Confirmed cases reach the annual report through a short chain of
passive reporting (@fig-pipeline): a clinician files a case report,
the Department reviews and registers it, and counts are released each
calendar year.

![Surveillance pipeline: clinician reports flow to the Department of Public Health and into the annual surveillance report.](images/surveillance-pipeline.png){#fig-pipeline fig-alt="Diagram of the surveillance pipeline, showing how clinicians report cases to the Department of Public Health, which reviews and registers them before releasing counts in the annual surveillance report."}

### Reportable conditions

A handful of vaccine-preventable diseases are reportable in Arcadonia,
each with a class and a maximum reporting window.

| Condition  | Class | Reporting window |
|------------|-------|------------------|
| Tetanus    | B     | 7 days           |
| Diphtheria | A     | 24 hours         |
| Pertussis  | B     | 7 days           |
